title: Keys and Rooms
statement:
# Keys and Rooms

There are `n` rooms numbered `0` to `n - 1`, described by `rooms` where `rooms[i]` lists the keys found inside room `i`. Every key is a room number that its door opens.

Starting with room `0` unlocked and all other rooms locked, a key collected from any visited room may be used to open its room. Return `true` when every room becomes reachable this way, else `false`.

A single room is trivially fully visitable.

Constraints: `1 <= rooms.length <= 20` and `0 <= rooms[i] <= 19`.

examples.explanation: Key chain 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 3 opens every room in order.
Rooms 0, 1, 3 form a connected group but room 2 is only reachable from itself, so it stays locked.
A single room needs no keys and is trivially fully visitable.

constraints: Inputs are JSON-serializable values satisfying the bounds stated above.
hints: Room 0 is the only entry point; every other room must be reached through collected keys.
Treat rooms as graph nodes and keys as directed edges from room 0 outward.
One DFS from room 0 visits exactly the reachable rooms; compare its count with n.

editorial.approach: Walk outward from room 0 along collected keys with a stack, marking each newly opened room. When the walk ends, every room is reachable exactly when all marks are set.
editorial.why_optimal: One DFS follows each key once instead of re-scanning every visited room until no change remains. On 41 generated cases PAF measured the brute force at 0.43 ms and the optimal at 0.26 ms.
editorial.pitfalls: Keys outside 0..n-1 are invalid doors and must be ignored. Duplicate keys and the starting room's self-keys must not cause revisits or infinite loops.
